Solution skeleton:
- Let D be any PPT distinguisher and let S_n = {z : D(z)=1}.
- Then |Pr[D(X_n)=1] − Pr[D(Y_n)=1]| = |Pr[X_n∈S_n] − Pr[Y_n∈S_n]|.
- By the max characterization of variation distance, |Pr[X_n∈S_n] − Pr[Y_n∈S_n]| ≤ Δ(X_n, Y_n).
- Statistical closeness gives Δ(X_n, Y_n) ≤ 1/p(n) for every positive polynomial p and all sufficiently large n.
- Hence for every D and every p, eventually the gap < 1/p(n): the ensembles are computationally indistinguishable (M2-2, COURSE.md §4).

Solution skeleton:
- Take $X_k = G(U_k)$ and $Y_k = U_{\ell(k)}$ in Definition 2.4 with $n = k$.
- Definition 2.1 says exactly that these two ensembles are computationally indistinguishable.
- §2.3.1: an ensemble indistinguishable from the uniform ensemble is called pseudorandom — so Definition 2.1 says $\{G(U_k)\}_k$ is pseudorandom.
- The ensembles are polynomial-time constructible (sample $s \leftarrow U_k$, output $G(s)$), so this is the non-trivial kind of indistinguishability the Primer is after.
